clue.text: Place for cleaning used to be focal point, given time inside

parts.note: was is the past tense of be, so 'used to be' gives WAS

indicators.note: inside tells us the time letter goes within the word for focal point

parts.note: a hub is the centre or focal point of activity

explanation.surface: A wistful note that a spot once at the heart of things, given time, became a laundry corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub of water for washing clothes is literally a place where cleaning happens.

clue.text: Moaning for what reason? Latest leader of government's interfering

indicators.note: interfering means getting in the middle, so these letters go inside the question word

parts.note: why asks for what reason
in means fashionable, the latest thing

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains, asking why the head of government keeps meddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Whingy is informal British for complaining or whining, so moaning is a synonym.

clue.text: Retiring attracts three of pop band worn-out

indicators.note: attracts means the shy word draws the band's letters into itself

parts.note: retiring means shy and reserved

indicators.note: three of means only three of the band's four letters are kept, dropping the last

parts.note: ABBA is the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A retiring person is drawn to three-quarters of a pop group, who look tired.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby clothes are threadbare and frayed through long use, so worn-out describes them.

clue.text: Underdeveloped regions with linguistics unit inspiring learner after degree

indicators.note: after means the word piece comes behind the degree

parts.note: a third is a low class of university degree

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the word takes the learner letter inside it

parts.note: a word is a basic unit of language
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A language student with a weak degree heads to poorer countries.
explanation.walkthrough: A third-class degree is the lowest honours grade at British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: The term once used for poorer nations is a label for economically underdeveloped parts of the globe.

clue.text: Sting's a poet

definitions.meaning: stings, as nettles do, meaning smarts or scorches

explanation.surface: The singer Sting is a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting looks like the singer; it is the verb, and the apostrophe-s stands for 'stings'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sting and to scorch both describe smarting pain, and Robert of that name is Scotland's poet.

clue.text: Rage about group of musicians being excessive

indicators.note: about means the word for rage goes round the orchestra's letters

parts.note: to fume is to rage with anger
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: Someone fumes at a band for overdoing things.
explanation.walkthrough: LSO, the London Symphony Orchestra, is a familiar crossword group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulsome praise or flattery is overdone, laid on too thickly, so excessive is a synonym.

clue.text: Knockout punch that brightens Independence Day party?

definitions.note: a light at an American party; the noun phrase stands for the object

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them down
to lamp someone is slang for punching them

explanation.surface: A knockout blow at a Fourth of July celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Independence Day points to the USA: this is the American name for what Britons call a standard lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall standing light in an American home would light up a Fourth of July gathering.

clue.text: Place where people go in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is as heard

parts.note: the loo is British slang for the toilet, where people go

explanation.surface: Where audience members head during the interval at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: In lieu of means in place of, so the French-derived word means place.

clue.text: Lion picked up around enclosure on recording system, sort of

indicators.note: around means the turned lion goes round the other letters
picked up means lifted, so in this down entry the lion's letters read upwards

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
a pen is an enclosure for animals
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A lion is lifted near its enclosure while a recording runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-reel tape is a type of audio recording format where tape runs between exposed spools.

clue.text: Guess the writer's boarding big car

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so the letters go inside the car

parts.note: an estate is a large car with a long rear load space
the writer's means 'the writer is', so I'M

explanation.surface: The writer guesses as they climb into a large car.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make a rough calculation, an informed guess.

clue.text: Island drizzle almost drenches queen from Asian country

indicators.note: drenches means the shortened rain soaks round the queen's letter
almost means the last letter of the word for drizzle is dropped

parts.note: drizzle is light rain
Q is the abbreviation for queen, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: A queen caught in island drizzle, having come from somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a country in western Asia, and the adjective describes anything from there.

clue.text: Old American boss regrets grassland rambling

indicators.note: rambling speech runs words together loosely, so this signals the two words said out loud as one

parts.note: regrets is RUES and South African grassland is VELDT

explanation.surface: A former US manager full of remorse while wandering across open plains.
explanation.walkthrough: VELDT is open grassland in southern Africa. Said together, 'rues veldt' sounds like the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin Roosevelt were both US presidents, past heads of the American nation.

clue.text: Proceed to offer trees to doctor in arid expanse

parts.note: to go is to proceed
a bid is an offer, as at auction

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of trees are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to go ahead, make a bid for some trees and tamper with them in a desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert in Mongolia and China, a dry, barren stretch of land.

clue.text: Revolutionary hurt by constant press

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A revolutionary injured by a persistent press campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to pack or press tightly into a space.

clue.text: It's a routine job to shut up dog burying bone

definitions.note: names the type of work; the answer is the noun for dull office labour

parts.note: to pen an animal is to shut it up

indicators.note: burying means the dog's letters surround the bone

parts.note: a pug is a small wrinkle-faced dog
the shin is the bone of the lower leg

explanation.surface: Penning up a dog that keeps burying bones is simply a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-pushing is dull routine clerical work, a tedious desk job.

clue.text: Badly soiled netball, not current sporting prize

indicators.note: badly means the letters of the fodder are put in a poor, jumbled order

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A grubby netball that is no longer in fashion being handed out as a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not current' removes the letter I from SOILED NETBALL before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lonsdale Belt is the trophy awarded to British boxing champions, a prize in sport.

clue.text: Stray autobus bypassing the odd arch in a meandering way

parts.note: to sin is to stray from the right way

indicators.note: bypassing the odd means skipping the first, third and other odd-numbered letters

parts.note: arch as an adjective means sly or knowing

explanation.surface: A stray bus goes round an odd arch on a winding route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like a structure the bus avoids; it is the adjective meaning roguish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuous means winding and curving, so the adverb says meandering.

clue.text: Unusual name in US baseball team remains

parts.note: odd means unusual

indicators.note: in means the name letter goes inside the team

parts.note: the Mets are the New York baseball team

explanation.surface: An odd name turns up on a US baseball team that is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftovers or scraps, the bits that remain.

clue.text: Crude and angry mostly, Charlie promoted domestic dispute

indicators.note: promoted means raised up, so in this down entry the letters read upwards

parts.note: raw means crude or unrefined

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is cut

parts.note: livid means furious
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A crude, furious Charlie wins a promotion amid a household row.
explanation.definitionFit: A civil war is fought within one country, a domestic conflict rather than a foreign one.

clue.text: Tube one takes to Epping, unfortunately meeting bore

parts.note: to bore a hole is to drill
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of Epping are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Londoner takes the Tube to Epping and, sadly, ends up with a bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground, whose Central line runs to Epping; here it is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilling pipe is a tube used to bore wells, so tube names its kind.

clue.text: Opulent duke showing amount of light flooding wings of estate

indicators.note: flooding means the light pours in between the outer letters
the wings of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: a lux is the unit of illuminance

explanation.surface: A wealthy duke shows off light pouring into the wings of his country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Something luxurious and lavish is opulent, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Wait on dry space in trailer

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the trailer

parts.note: an ad, or trailer, advertises a coming film
TT means teetotal, off alcohol
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: Waiting in a dry patch inside a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' looks like a vehicle; it is a film preview, an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait on someone is to serve them, which is what attending to them means.

clue.text: Maiden with intention to cause wound

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
an aim is an intention or purpose

explanation.surface: A young woman who sets out meaning to injure someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to injure badly, so wound as a verb is a close synonym.

clue.text: Kid is to return medical device that's fixed

parts.note: to kid is to con or fool

indicators.note: to return means the word is goes back the other way

parts.note: a stent is a tube inserted to hold open a blocked artery

explanation.surface: A child gives back a piece of hospital kit that has been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the verb meaning to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consistent is unchanging, steady and settled, so fixed is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Way of communicating quietly in Scottish isle

indicators.note: in means the quiet letter sits inside the island

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Talking softly on a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: The internet video-call service is a means of talking to people at a distance.

clue.text: Lime zest scratching half dishes

indicators.note: scratching half means scraping off the outer half of the letters, two from each end, leaving the core

explanation.surface: Grating lime zest onto half the plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Meze are small Mediterranean appetiser plates served together as a spread.

clue.text: State what first-year schoolboy might wear

definitions.meaning: a state of the USA, home of Bruce Springsteen
a new pupil would wear a brand new pullover from the school uniform

explanation.surface: Say what a boy starting secondary school would put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like the verb 'say'; it is a US state. A jersey is a British word for a pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, the state's name describes a freshly bought pullover worn by a newcomer.

clue.text: Getting employment that is besetting many students

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so the letters for that is go round the students

parts.note: IE stands for id est, Latin for that is
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Finding a job when crowds of students are hemming you in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being used is getting employed, so the phrase describes a thing put to work.

clue.text: Theatre work's good when involved in certain lines

indicators.note: involved in means the good letter goes inside the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines a train runs on

explanation.surface: An actor's work is good when it fits within certain lines of the script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' and 'lines' point to the stage, but this is an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is where surgeons work, so operations done there are theatre work.

clue.text: E? A+ is more likely for this person

definitions.text: A+ is more likely for this person

parts.note: split into two words, 'head of egg' is its first letter, which is the single letter printed here

explanation.surface: A school grade query: would this student get an E, or more likely an A-plus?
explanation.walkthrough: E is also a poor exam grade, set against the top mark A+.
explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual swot would be expected to earn top marks rather than a failing grade.
